subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency & concurrency details
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jai Singh <jai.singh@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput / latency targets

Hi Jai — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size an initial inference footprint for FinEx: 

Summary of what I heard today:
- Primary workload: real-time transaction summarization + assistant suggestions for traders.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 150ms for tail latency on single-request end-to-end (streaming acceptable; prefer seeing first tokens within ~50ms).
- Concurrency/Throughput: expected steady-state ~15-25 concurrent request QPS; occasional bursts up to ~120 QPS for ~20-60s.
- Typical request: ~200-350 tokens output, ~50-100 tokens input. Streaming desired for progressive UI updates.
- Security: FinEx requires SOC2 evidence and private VPC option for production.

Questions / ask from our side to finalize sizing: 
1) Can you confirm average tokens per request (input + output) and typical variance?
2) For the burst profile, is 120 QPS the absolute peak and how often (daily/week/month)?
3) Are there strict concurrency limits per user/session we should know about (long-running sessions with KV cache reuse, etc.)?
4) Please share a short sample workload (CSV or jsonl) with timestamped requests if available — even a 1-2 hour sample will help.

Next steps we propose:
- You share workload sample (CSV) and any SLO docs (we referenced SOC2 earlier).
- We run an internal throughput model and reply with tokens/sec estimates, target GPUs/pod count, and a cost/latency tradeoff.

Attaching the throughput reference doc we discussed (redwood_throughput_reference.pdf) and a small sample CSV template.

Thanks — I’ll loop Neha and Marissa for sizing once we have the sample.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_throughput_reference.pdf (PDF, 480KB), workload_template.csv (CSV)

From: Jai Singh <jai.singh@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: FinEx SRE <sre@finex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput / latency targets

Thanks, Rafael — appreciate the recap. A few answers and a sample attached.

Answers: 
- Average tokens per request: output ~260 tokens, input ~80 tokens (so ~340 tokens total average). Variance: P90 ~520 tokens, P99 ~1.1k tokens.
- Burst profile: 120 QPS is our observed peak during market opens; happens 2-3x per trading day, lasts typically 20-45s. Daily peak events roughly concentrated in US market open and major news events.
- Sessions: users can open long-lived sessions, but most requests are independent (we do have session affinity for KV cache in ~10% of flows).
- Attached: finex_workload_sample.csv (~1 hour of timestamped requests from last week).

Streaming: yes — streaming is required for the trader UI to see progressive updates.

Let me know if you need anything else. We expect to start a pilot in ~3-4 weeks and would like an initial sizing recommendation before procurement.

Thanks,
Jai Singh
Head of Trading Systems, FinEx
jai.singh@finex.com

Attachment: finex_workload_sample.csv (CSV, 92KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jai Singh <jai.singh@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput / latency targets

Great — got the sample, thanks. We’ll run a quick pass and return a preliminary sizing note by EOD tomorrow. Initial thoughts from eyeballing the sample:

- With average ~340 tokens/request and a 120 QPS peak, that implies ~40.8k tokens/sec at peak (340 * 120).
- Accounting for model overhead and headroom (KV reuse, burst safety), we typically plan for 1.5x-2x padding => ~60-82k tokens/sec effective capacity for peak.
- Streaming means we care about time-to-first-token; we’ll include a low-latency config and a cost-optimized config (slightly higher latency but lower GPU count).

Action items from us:
- Marissa/Neha: can you run the throughput model with the attached sample and return a short sizing recommendation (tokens/sec -> GPUs / pods / concurrency settings)?
- Jai: any SRE contact we should include for procurement / network setup?

Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput / latency targets

Quick internal sizing note (based on finex_workload_sample.csv):

Assumptions used:
- Avg tokens/request: 340 (Jai reported)
- Peak QPS: 120 sustained for 30-45s; steady-state QPS: 20
- Target tail SLO: 95th <= 150ms (stream-first within ~50ms)
- Model: 13B quantized variant (latency profile aligns with their accuracy needs)

Preliminary numbers (rounding up for headroom):
- Peak tokens/sec (raw): 340 * 120 = 40,800 tokens/sec
- Engineering padding: 2.0x (burst + system overhead) -> target capacity ~82,000 tokens/sec
- Concurrent inflight requests at peak (assume average server-side processing window ~600ms due to streaming): ~72 concurrent requests 

Suggested starting deployment (pilot):
- 2 inference pods, each serving ~41k tokens/sec (multi-GPU / partitioning recommended).
- GPU recommendation: 8 x A100-80GB per pod (or equivalent partitioning on 4 x H100 if available); we can size down to 4 x A100 with higher latency and lower headroom.
- Autoscale policy: keep steady-state at 1 pod; scale to 2 pods at 50 QPS, 3 pods at 90 QPS, 4 pods at 110+ QPS (fast scale-up for short bursts).
- Streaming config: low-latency intra-token flushing, small decode batches (to preserve first-token latency).

Next steps (for pilot):
- Rafael: share this with Jai and request SRE contact and procurement timing.
- Neha: I'll prepare a short cost estimate and expected latency numbers for the two configs (low-latency / cost-optimized).

Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
